parole.significato: a collection of twigs, branches or small trees sunk in the water to attract perch fish
parole.testo: abbor + bråte, first part from Old Danish aghborre (“perch”) and Old Swedish aghborre, aborre (“perch”), the beginning of the word comes from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp, pointed”) + the end of the word comes from Old Norse borrablað, from Proto-Germanic *burzô. Last part from Old Norse broti

parole.significato: the perch family; Percidae (a taxonomic family within order Perciformes)
parole.testo: abbor + familie, first part from Old Danish aghborre (“perch”) and Old Swedish aghborre, aborre (“perch”), the beginning of the word comes from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp, pointed”) + the end of the word comes from Old Norse borrablað, from Proto-Germanic *burzô. Last part familie (“family”)

abbor + fiske, first part from Old Danish aghborre (“perch”) and Old Swedish aghborre, aborre (“perch”), the beginning of the word comes from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp, pointed”) + the end of the word comes from Old Norse borrablað, from Proto-Germanic *burzô. Last part from Old Norse fiski

parole.significato: a perch fisher (a person who fishes perch)
parole.testo: abbor + fisker, first part from Old Danish aghborre (“perch”) and Old Swedish aghborre, aborre (“perch”), the beginning of the word comes from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp, pointed”) + the end of the word comes from Old Norse borrablað, from Proto-Germanic *burzô. Last part from Old Norse fisk

parole.significato: a pondweed (any plant in the Potamogeton family, a diverse and worldwide genus)
parole.testo: abbor + gress, first part from Old Danish aghborre (“perch”) and Old Swedish aghborre, aborre (“perch”), the beginning of the word comes from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp, pointed”) + the end of the word comes from Old Norse borrablað, from Proto-Germanic *burzô. Last part from Old Norse gras

parole.significato: a fish trap for fishing perch
parole.testo: abbor + ruse, first part from Old Danish aghborre (“perch”) and Old Swedish aghborre, aborre (“perch”), the beginning of the word comes from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp, pointed”) + the end of the word comes from Old Norse borrablað, from Proto-Germanic *burzô. Last part possibly from a Celti

parole.significato: a fry of perch (young perch fishlings)
parole.testo: abbor + yngel, first part from Old Danish aghborre (“perch”) and Old Swedish aghborre, aborre (“perch”), the beginning of the word comes from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp, pointed”) + the end of the word comes from Old Norse borrablað, from Proto-Germanic *burzô. Last part from the verb yngle
From Old Danish ark, arken, arkens, through Middle Low German or Low German arkener (“breast protection”), from Old French arquiere (“shooting range”).
From Old Danish egn, from Old Norse eign.

parole.significato: a widow (woman whose husband has died)
parole.testo: From Old Danish ænkia (“widow”), Old East Norse variant of Old Norse ekkja, from Proto-Germanic *ainakjǭ.

parole.significato: a queen dowager; the widow of a king
parole.testo: From enke (“widow”) + dronning (“queen”), literally “widow queen”. The first element enke (“widow”) is from Old Danish ænkia (“widow”), corresponding to Old Norse ekkja (“widow”), from Proto-Germanic *ainakjǭ (“widow”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₁óynos (“one”). The second element dronnin

parole.significato: an empress dowager; the widow of an emperor, especially in historical or foreign contexts
parole.testo: From enke (“widow”) + keiserinne (“empress”), literally “widow empress”. The first element enke (“widow”) is from Old Danish ænkia (“widow”), from Proto-Germanic *ainakjǭ (“widow”), based on *ainagaz (“only, sole”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₁óynos (“one”). The second element keiserinne

parole.significato: to distort, corrupt, garble, mutilate (e.g. a text)

parole.testo: Developed from Old Danish mon, from Old Norse móa (“to digest”), from Proto-Germanic *meuk- or *mūk-, from Proto-Indo-European *mewg- (“slimy, slippery”).
From a diminutive form of Old Danish mussel, from Latin musculus.

Influenced by Old Danish slenghe and Danish slænge, from Old Norse slængja, slyngja, causative of slængva, sløngva, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *slangwijaną. Compare Norwegian Nynorsk slengja, which retains the diphthong from Old Norse; also Icelandic slengja, Old Swedish slængia → Swedish slänga
From Old Danish spørsmaal. By surface analysis, spørre + mål. Compare to modern Danish spørgsmål.

parole.significato: drunkard, a person who is constantly out drinking (alcohol)
parole.testo: ture + basse, first part from Old Danish ture (“to go on a warpath or ravage”). Last part from Old Norse bassi (“bear”).
